knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)

## A question worth asking

\vspace{1em}
\large

"What are the important problems of your field?"

\vspace{0.5em}

"If what you are doing is not important, and if you don't think it is going to lead to something important, why are you ... working on it?"

\vspace{1em}
\normalsize

-- Richard Hamming, ["You and Your Research"](https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~robins/YouAndYourResearch.html) (1986)

\vspace{0.5em}
\small

Tyler Cowen's version: ["What are the most important unsolved problems in your field?"](https://marginalrevolution.com/marginalrevolution/2017/01/important-unsolved-problems-field.html)

## The most important question in our field

- What will meaningfully reduce consumption of meat and animal products?
  - What works best?
  - What's most cost-effective?
  - Whom should we target with what?

## I wrote one paper that addresses this directly {.t}

A [meta-analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.appet.2025.108233) of interventions intended to reduce consumption of meat and animal products. Basically nothing works :(

## But most of my papers are not about this {.t}

Smaller, more foundational: measurement, small changes, [how big effects should be](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/p/expect-1-2-pp-changes-and-you-wont)

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
[TACOS](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foodqual.2026.105931): adding plant-based options to a Chipotle-like menu cut meat by \~1 pp. per option

\includegraphics[width=\linewidth, height=0.55\textheight, keepaspectratio]{images/tacos-paper-title.png}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

## Why do I do this? {.t}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
\small\vspace{0.5em}

- [Our field isn't mature yet](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/svjqgyFuFQ34qSgmw/animal-welfare-has-an-evidence-problem) (not the way economics is)
- Really basic methodological questions are still open
- So typical studies can't tell us what meaningfully reduces consumption
  - [The design and measurement](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/p/the-hard-part-is-defining-your-estimand) aren't there yet
- We can crack this from many angles, and many of us should
  - Even if it looks like we're dodging the most important question
:::

:::
:::::

## Fixing the whole field is really hard

- Thank goodness Kristof Dhont et al. ([PHAIR](https://phairsociety.org/)) are working on that!!
- But personally I think it's fine to either:
  - evaluate the incrementalist stuff that actually gets deployed in the real world, or
  - do more meta-level work on [measurement error](https://regressiontothemeat.substack.com/p/i-believe-self-reported-meat-consumption) and design
  - (tastes may vary)
- Not working on the big question? Why not? What's your theory of change?
- Thanks!
